# MADRank for DSH
> **Track your AI usage. See how you rank.**
**English** | 简体中文
MADRank is an AI Usage & Ranking plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). It turns your DSH activity into
a private local dashboard — Today / 7-Day history / Top models / Streak — and, if you explicitly opt
in, an anonymous global **7-Day Token Race** based on real usage.
The core principle is simple: **local tracking runs by default, global ranking is an explicit opt-in
, uploads only happen for finished UTC days, and only aggregated usage is ever sent.**
Left: sidebar MADRank card (real local data) · Right: the Settings tab inside the same card

**1. Local AI Usage Dashboard** (works fully offline, no ranking required)

* **Today** — today's usage
* **7-Day / 30-Day History** — recent 7-day / 30-day trends
* **Top Mode

against your own 7-day baseline
* **RANK** — global rank status
* **Cached Tokens** — tracked separ
ately from the ranking metric

**2. 7-Day Token Race** (the core competitive metric)
> **7-Day Total** — your primary tokens over the last **7 UTC days**.

## Privacy by Design
Local tracking and global sync are separated at the architecture level.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**Never uploaded:** prompts, responses, tool arguments, individual request payloads, same-day usage.
**Uploaded:** daily, per-model aggregated usage only.
Two deletion controls live in the card's Settings tab (both require confirmation):
- **Clear local data** — removes this machine's local statistics from the clearing moment on; days b

efore it no longer appear in the card and are no longer uploaded.
- **Delete uploaded ranking data**
— asks MADRank to delete the anonymous daily rows already submitted from this installation; local s
tatistics stay untouched.
The anonymous share token is kept in the DSH credential store when the profile provides one, so `~/.
madrank/usage/global-rank.json` no longer contains it in plaintext (files fall back to the old behav
ior only when the credential service is absent).
## Usage Accuracy
MADRank does not invent a second token-accounting logic. It uses DSH's **session projection** as the
data source and reconciles aggregation against an independent reference token-meter. A real-session
reconciliation run:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The suite covers streaming replacement, waterfall tool traffic, cross-midnight bucketing and `(turn,
step)` replacement semantics. Goal: stay consistent with DSH's own token meter.
## Installation
> A DSH plugin is mounted from a **profile**. Two things must both be true, or the plugin silently d

oes nothing:
> 1. the package is **declared/installed** in the profile (`package.json` + `node_modul
> The published package ships the Host half **compiled to JavaScript** (`dist/host/`) and the browse
r half prebuilt (`dist/client.js`) — consumers need no build step. (Node refuses to type-strip TypeS
cript inside `node_modules`, which is why installed packages must not point `main` at a `.ts` file.)

## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]
DSH session logs are the source of truth; the plugin reads `sessionProjections` (never SQLite direct
ly), keeps a rebuildable local cache, and keeps daily sync fully isolated from local statistics. All
DSH coupling lives in `src/compat.ts` — verifiable via `npm run verify:dsh`.
Integration follows the current official plugin model (`cordis-plugin-development` references): the
bundle declares `dsh.bundle.patch`; the Host exports `apply(ctx, config)` with `inject` plus a schem
astery `Config`, awaits the 0.2.x `sessionProjections.register()` handle and disposes it on unload,
and prefers the official `timer` service. The Client is a lazy `window.__ModuleLoader__` factory tha
t registers two additive slots — `settings.section` (the configuration page) and `sidebar.footer.act
ion` (the Quick View entry) — and reads session data through the slot's standard `useSessions` props
on` (the Quick View entry) — and reads session data through the slot's standard `useSessions` props.
Non-negotiables: never fork DSH · never read internal SQLite directly · never duplicate token-meter
semantics · never create an independent session event pipeline · never upload same-day usage · never
upload prompts/responses/tool arguments · never let global sync block local statistics.
